dataset.description: In this data set, the obtained results of sample weight changes and various physicochemical methods, e.g., ATR-FTIR spectroscopy, scanning electron microscopy – energy dispersive X-ray spectroscopy (SEM-EDX), TG/DSC, and secondary ion mass spectrometry (SIMS), will be summarised for the pressed ACB pellets before and after storage and thermal treatment experiments.

distribution.title: In the framework of WP-2, the storage experiment of the pressed ACB pellets after thermal pre-treatment will be carried out in sealed desiccators at room temperature using air atmosphere with low (≤10 RH%), normal (~30 RH%), and high humidity (≥70 RH%). The various humidities will be obtained using relevant sorbents, e.g., sulphuric acid (H2SO4) with different concentrations, while humidity and temperature will be measured using Uni-T-333S humidity tester, but CO2 concentration – using LogIT Voyager Microsense CO2 sensor. The weight changes of the pressed pellets after different times (up to one month) will be monitored using analytical balance Precisa, whereas the surface chemical composition and microstructure will be studied using ATR-FTIR and SEM-EDX (Zeiss Auriga). The thickness and chemical composition of the formed layer of various chemisorption products will be investigated using SIMS (HIDEN analytical Workstation). Afterwards, the pressed pellets after the storage experiment will be stepwise thermally treated using the thermal annealing system up to 800 °C for at least 1 h hold at a maximal temperature in vacuum (heating rate: 5 °C/min, incremental step: 100 °C). The content of sorbed and chemisorbed gaseous compounds in the pressed pellets before and after gradual thermal treatment will be determined using TG/DSC, whereas surface chemical composition and microstructure will be studied using ATR-FTIR and SEM-EDX. The obtained results (i.e., raw data) will be stored in relevent database and afterwards will be processed using Excel or Origin software.

dataset.title: WP-2: “Characterisation of the pressed ACB pellets after storage and thermal treatment experiments”

dataset.description: In this data set, the obtained results of various physico-chemical methods, e.g., powder X-ray diffractometry (PXRD), attenuated total reflectance – Fourier transform infrared (ATR-FTIR) spectroscopy, and  thermogravimetry/differential scanning calorimetry (TG/DSC), will be summarised for the pressed ACB pellets before storage and thermal treatment experiments.

distribution.title: In the framework of WP-1, the produced ACB pebbles will be powdered using an agate mortar and afterwards pressed into pellets with a diameter of approx. 10 mm and a thickness of approx. 1 mm using uniaxial hydraulic press (Specac AtlasTM). The load and time of the pellets will be selected according to the situation. Subsequently, the pressed pellets will be thermally pre-treated at approx. 800 °C for 1 h in vacuum. The thermal pre-treatment will be conducted using thermal annealing system, which consists of Nabertherm horizontal split-type tube furnace RSH 50/500/13, ceramic tube, gas supply system with vacuum-tight stainless steel water-cooled flanges, Leybold SOGEVAC single-stage oil-sealed rotary vane pump, HYFRA Air-type water recooler LWK 21-S, Leybold digital vacuum meter Thermovac TM101, and charge control with temperature measurement in the working tube. The crystalline phase composition of the fabricated ACB pebbles will be analysed using PXRD (Bruker Advanced). The surface chemical composition of the pressed pellets before and after thermal pre-treatment will be analysed using ATR-FTIR (Bruker Vertex 70v). The weight changes and crystalline phase transitions will be analysed using TG/DSC (SETARAM – LABSYS Evo). The obtained results (i.e., raw data) will be stored in relevent database and afterwards will be processed using Excel or Origin software.

dataset.title: WP-1: “Preparation and characterisation of the pressed ACB pellets for storage and thermal treatment experiments”

dataset.description: In this data set, the obtained results of electron paramagnetic resonance (EPR) spectroscopy will be summarised for the irradiated pressed ACB pellets before and after storage and thermal treatment experiments.

distribution.title: In the framework of WP-3, the irradiation experiments using X-rays of the pressed ACB pellets before and after storage and thermal treatment experiments will be carried out simultenuuesly using a custom-built setup equipped with an X-ray tube (tungsten anode, anode voltage: 45 kV, anode current: 10 mA, irradiation time: 30 min, room temperature, air atmosphere). The absorbed dose will be approx. 1 kGy. After the irradiation, the formed and accumulated paramagnetic radiation-induced defect centres will be analysed using EPR spectrometry (Bruker Elexsys-II E500). Spectra were recorded at room temperature with microwave radiation at a frequency of 9.83 GHz, using a power range of 10-100 mW, a magnetic field modulation frequency of 100 kHz, and a modulation amplitude of 0.4 mT.

dataset.title: WP-3: “Irradiation of the pressed ACB pellets before and after storage and thermal treatment experiments using X-rays and characterisation with EPR spectroscopy”

dmp.description:
The Data Management Plan (DMP) is developed in the framework of the project No. 5.2.1.1.i.0/2/24/I/CFLA/007 "Internal and External Consolidation of the University of Latvia" of the second round of the Consolidation and Governance Change Implementation Grants within Investment 5.2.1.1.i "Research, Development and Consolidation Grants" under Reform 5.2.1.r "Higher Education and Science Excellence and Governance Reform" of Reform and Investment Strand 5.2 of the Latvian Recovery and Resilience Mechanism Plan "Ensuring Change in the Governance Model of Higher Education Institutions", postdoctoral research grant project No. LU-BA-PG-2024/1-0007 "Influence of sample handling conditions on radiation-induced effects in biphasic tritium breeding material for future thermonuclear fusion reactors" (project manager: Dr. chem. Artūrs Zariņš, 1st September 2024 – 31st August 2025, 61 380.00 EUR).
Summary of the postdoctoral reasearch grant project: Advanced ceramic breeder (ACB) pebbles consisting of lithium orthosilicate and the mechanical stability strengthening phase lithium metatitanate are developed and extensively tested as the European Union’s reference solid-state material for tritium breeding in future thermonuclear fusion reactors. In this applied research project, the influence of sample handling conditions on radiation-induced effects in the biphasic ACB pellets will be investigated using various physico-chemical methods in order to develop recommendations for future irradiation experiments using accelerated ions. The main scientific findings will be submitted for publication in at least one international peer-reviewed thermonuclear fusion-relevant journal or conference proceeding, which is indexed in the Web of Science Core Collection, SCOPUS or ERIH PLUS databases. At least one project proposal will be prepared in cooperation with local and international partners for submission in a local or international call for research and development projects, which is necessary for the further funding of this scientific research direction at the University of Latvia. This research project will contribute to the Smart Specialisation Strategy (RIS3) area “Smart energetics” of the Republic of Latvia and the development of international nuclear energy sector, including for participation in the EUROfusion consortium.
